# Refactor packCoins to left-align coin placements

**Parent:** CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I — Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right.

## Goal
Change `packCoins` from centre-relative placement to left-aligned placement so coins start at the left edge of the grid and grow rightwards.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `packCoins` placements start at `w/2` (left edge) and extend to `w/2 + finalGridW - w` (right edge) for X; Y remains vertically centred within the available height.
- [ ] For 1 coin, placement.x equals `w/2` (the first coin sits at the left edge of the grid).
- [ ] All existing packing behaviour (column growth 5→10→15, shrink, overlap, height-fit scaling) is preserved.
- [ ] All placements fit within `availableWidth`: `0 ≤ p.x ≤ availableWidth - coinSize` for every placement.
- [ ] Unit tests updated to assert left-aligned placement values instead of centre-relative absolute values.

## Implementation
- In `packCoins` (coin-grid.ts ~line 202), change the X placement formula:
  - Old: `x: col * (w + s) - finalGridW / 2 + w / 2`
  - New: `x: col * (w + s) + w / 2`
- Update the `packCoins` doc comment to reflect left-aligned packing.
- Update test assertions in `coin-grid.test.ts` that check `Math.abs(p.x) ≤ availableWidth / 2` to check `0 ≤ p.x` and `p.x + coinSize ≤ availableWidth`.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` — `packCoins` layout formula
- `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts` — placement assertions

## Dependencies
None — this is the first task.

# Update createCoinGrid defaults to left-anchored position

**Parent:** CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I — Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right.

## Goal
Change `createCoinGrid` default anchor point and available region so the coin grid renders on the left side of the card instead of the bottom-right quadrant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Default anchorX is at the left edge of the card minus a small inset (`-cardW/2 + leftInset`, default leftInset=8px), so the grid's leftmost coin aligns with the card's left inset.
- [ ] Default anchorY remains at `cardH/4` (bottom quarter of card), keeping the grid in the lower portion.
- [ ] Default `availableWidth` is `cardW - leftInset * 2` (full card width minus left/right insets), giving coins maximum horizontal space.
- [ ] `availableHeight` remains `cardH/2` (same as current default, grid height fits within this).
- [ ] The grid container stays parented to the card and moves with it (existing `createCoinGrid` contract preserved).
- [ ] Existing `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomePhases` call (`createCoinGrid(s, card)`) works without modification — defaults are correct.

## Implementation
- In `createCoinGrid` (coin-grid.ts ~line 293), change the default values:
  - `availableWidth = cardW - leftInset * 2` (was `cardW / 2`)
  - `anchorX = -cardW / 2 + leftInset` (was `cardW / 4`)
  - `anchorY` stays `cardH / 4`
  - `availableHeight` stays `cardH / 2`
- Add constants: `COIN_GRID_LEFT_INSET = 8`, `COIN_GRID_BOTTOM_INSET = 12`
- Update `CoinGridOptions.availableWidth` comment: "Region the grid must fit within (defaults to full card width minus left/right insets)."
- Update `createCoinGrid` doc comment: "Defaults: the grid is left-aligned within the card face (`availableWidth` defaults to the full card width minus insets, and the anchor defaults to the left edge)."

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` — `createCoinGrid` defaults and doc comments
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — verify default call still correct (no per-slot override needed)

## Dependencies
- CG-0MU9JVGNM0051ZVA — Refactor packCoins to left-align coin placements (must complete first)

# Update coin-grid tests and documentation for left-aligned layout

**Parent:** CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I — Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right.

## Goal
Update all coin-grid unit tests, browser tests, and VFX-scaling tests to reflect the new left-aligned contract, and update any in-code documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `coin-grid.test.ts` — `packCoins` placement assertions updated:
  - "never clips" test: check `p.x ≥ 0` and `p.x + coinSize ≤ availableWidth` instead of `Math.abs(p.x) ≤ availableWidth / 2`.
  - "shrinks coins" test: check `Math.max(...placements.map(p => p.x)) + coinSize ≤ availableWidth` instead of `Math.abs(p.x)`.
  - "overlap" test: same replacement of absolute-value checks with left-edge checks.
- [ ] `coin-grid.test.ts` — add explicit left-alignment assertions:
  - For 1 coin: `layout.placements[0].x === w / 2` (or within epsilon).
  - For N coins: `layout.placements[0].x === w / 2` and `layout.placements[N-1].x` is the rightmost placement.
- [ ] `coin-grid.browser.test.ts` — update "renders packed coins" test: check icons within left-aligned bounds instead of centre-relative half-extents.
  - Old: `Math.abs(icon.x + grid.container.x) ≤ 70 + 1`
  - New: verify coins are within the card's left-aligned region.
- [ ] `coin-grid.browser.test.ts` — update "never clips: many coins on a small card" test: adjust bounds to left-aligned region.
- [ ] `coin-vfx-scaling.test.ts` — verify no changes needed (pure function, unaffected by layout); if it references packCoins placement values, update accordingly.
- [ ] `coin-grid.ts` header comment updated: "Packing policy: the grid starts at the left edge of the card and grows rightwards (row-major, left→right, top→bottom)."
- [ ] `npm test -- --project unit tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] `npm test -- --project browser tests/main-street/coin-grid.browser.test.ts` passes.

## Implementation
- Update `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts`:
  - Change the "never clips" test from `Math.abs(p.x) ≤ area.availableWidth / 2 + 1e-6` to `p.x ≥ 0` and `p.x + coinSize ≤ area.availableWidth + 1e-6`.
  - Change "shrinks coins" test similarly.
  - Change "overlap" test similarly.
  - Add new test: "coins are left-aligned: first coin at w/2 from grid origin".
- Update `tests/main-street/coin-grid.browser.test.ts`:
  - "renders packed coins" test: replace `Math.abs(icon.x + grid.container.x) ≤ 70 + 1` with left-aligned bounds check.
  - "never clips" small card test: verify coins within left-aligned card region.
- Update `coin-grid.ts` header comment to reflect left-aligned packing policy.

## Key Files
- `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts` — unit test assertions
- `tests/main-street/coin-grid.browser.test.ts` — browser test assertions
- `tests/main-street/coin-vfx-scaling.test.ts` — VFX scaling (verify no changes)
- `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` — header comment

## Dependencies
- CG-0MU9JVGNM0051ZVA — Refactor packCoins to left-align coin placements

# Problem statement

The contextual first-bank hint overlay (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) fires during the tutorial when the player ends a turn with spare actions, creating a "dead end" that interrupts tutorial progression and confuses the tutorial state machine. The hint is designed for normal gameplay and should not fire while the tutorial is active.

## Users

- **New players** completing the Main Street tutorial — they expect a linear, guided experience. An unexpected banking hint overlay mid-tutorial interrupts this flow, potentially showing a stale or completed tutorial step after the hint is dismissed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Banking hint does not fire during tutorial:** The contextual first-bank hint trigger in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` must check that `tutorialController.isActive` is `false` (i.e., the tutorial is not active). The hint must never fire while the tutorial overlay is showing or a tutorial step is pending.
2. **Banking hint fires in normal gameplay:** The hint continues to fire exactly once when a non-tutorial player ends a turn with `actionsRemaining > 0`, respecting the persistence flag (`hasSeenBankingHint`).
3. **No regression to tutorial flow:** Existing tutorial steps, overlay lifecycle, and step progression remain unchanged. The tutorial still completes through all 26 steps without interruption from the banking hint.
4. **No regression to banking hint:** The hint still triggers correctly in normal gameplay after the tutorial is complete (on the first end-turn with spare actions).
5. **All tests pass:** Existing tutorial unit and browser tests pass; no new failures introduced.

## Constraints

- **Minimal change:** Only the trigger condition in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` needs modification (one logical operator change). No new fields, no structural changes.
- **Tutorial-layer only:** The fix is entirely within Main Street's tutorial wiring; no core-engine, card-system, or UI component changes.
- **Existing banking hint implementation preserved:** The `BANKING_HINT_STEP`, `renderBankingHint()`, and `TutorialState` banking hint flag remain unchanged.

## Existing state

- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** implemented the contextual first-bank hint with the following trigger in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()`:
  ```ts
  if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0) {
      pendingBankingHint = true;
      // persist flag via TutorialState
  }
  ```
- This condition fires when the tutorial is **active** AND the player has spare actions.
- The `renderBankingHint()` method saves the current tutorial step, shows the banking hint overlay, and on dismiss tries to restore the saved step — but if the tutorial step has already advanced (e.g., T6 End Turn completed), the restoration shows a stale step, creating the "dead end."
- The intent from the original brief (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) was that the hint fires **once per save** on the first bankable end-turn — but the implementation does not distinguish between tutorial and normal gameplay contexts.

## Desired change

Change the trigger condition in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` from:
```ts
if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)
```
to:
```ts
if (!tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)
```

This ensures the banking hint only fires in normal gameplay (after the tutorial is complete), never during the tutorial.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — One-line fix: invert the `tut?.isActive` check in the banking hint trigger (endTurn path, ~line 221).

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** (completed, merged) — Main Street: tutorial coverage for action banking (parent feature that introduced the contextual first-bank hint).
- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (completed, merged) — Main Street: action banking (engine-level banking logic).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** If the producer believes the banking hint should also fire during the tutorial (e.g., as an optional teaching moment), that would require a different design — but the title and description indicate this is clearly unintended.
- **No edge cases:** The banking hint has a one-shot persistence flag; if the hint never fires during the tutorial (which is the fix), it will fire on the player's first non-tutorial end-turn with spare actions — this is the intended behaviour.

# Add a Charity Shop business card (MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL) — Intake brief

## Problem statement

Main Street has no charity shop: a low-cost, Culture-synergy business that trades a modest income for a steady reputation trickle. The producer has specified the card's core economy (1.5 income/turn, 0.15 reputation/turn, cost 3 at the pre-scale convention), and this work adds the card to the pool so players gain an early reputation-leaning Culture business at tier 2.

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a player**, I can buy a Charity Shop for 300 coins and place it on the street, where it produces a small income and a steady reputation gain each turn, giving me an early Culture-synergy building with a reputation focus.
- **As a player**, I expect the Charity Shop to participate in Culture adjacency synergy like other Culture businesses (Bookshop, Craft Shop), so I can cluster it with my Culture cards.
- **As a maintainer**, I expect the new card to be a first-class registered template — present in the CSV, the tier/progression system, generated metadata and card art — with all template-count and consistency tests updated rather than special-cased.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data.** `src/card-data.csv` contains a new business row with exactly: `family = business`, `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`, `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 150`, `synergyTypes = Culture`, `upgradePath = Charity Shop`, `maxLevel = 1`, `reputationPerTurn = 15`, `ongoingCost = 75`, `tier = 2`, plus a non-empty `description` and `art_notes`.
2. **Registered template.** The card is loaded by `MainStreetCards.ts` as a business template, is available at tier 2 through the tier/`CARD_TIER_MAP` progression, and appears in the business deck built by `createBusinessDeck()`.
3. **Generated metadata and art.** `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` lists `biz-charity-shop` under `expandedCardIds.business`, and `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` produces `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-charity-shop.svg`; both are committed.
4. **Tests.** Automated tests assert the Charity Shop's `cost`, `baseIncome`, `reputationPerTurn`, `ongoingCost`, `synergyTypes` and `tier`, and every hardcoded count affected by adding one business template is updated:
   - business-template count `30 → 31` in `game-state.test.ts` (`BUSINESS_TEMPLATE_COUNT`), `expanded-card-pool.test.ts`, `group-a-business-expansion.test.ts` (test title/comment too), and the `createBusinessDeck(1).length` assertions in the `group-b`…`group-f` expansion tests;
   - aggregate pool totals in `meta-progression.test.ts`: tier-12 `cumulativeCardIds` `173 → 174` and unique base-id `allBaseIds.size` `165 → 166`;
   - the hardcoded tier-2 synergy snapshot in `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` becomes `{ Commerce: 2, Service: 1, Culture: 1 }`.
   The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (business table, deck-size/expansion counts, synergy-type coverage) and any relevant README or docs-site entries. **Note:** `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **×100 integer economy** (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6): all coin/reputation CSV values are integers at 100× the design scale — `cost 300`, `baseIncome 150`, `reputationPerTurn 15`. No fractional values anywhere in the CSV.
- **Ongoing cost convention** (CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE): businesses pay ¼ of purchase price per turn (min 25), so `ongoingCost = 75`; the card is charged this while in hand or on the street.
- **Card text must match data** (`card-text-data-consistency` test): the `description` reputation figure must equal the `reputationPerTurn` value and the synergy sentence must match the Culture synergy.
- **Tier-2 synergy balance** (`tier-synergy-balance.test.ts`, ≤2× ratio): tier 2 becomes Commerce 2 / Service 1 / Culture 1 — ratio 2.0, which passes.
- **Tier family balance** (`tier-family-balance.test.ts`, ≤46% per family): tier 2 business share becomes 4/22 ≈ 18.2% — passes.
- **Producer-specified cost override:** the balance curve (`tier*2 + 2 + baseIncome*4 + …`) would price this card higher than 300; the producer's explicit `cost 3` (300) takes precedence and is recorded as a deliberate manual override, not a curve result.

## Existing state

- There is **no** charity shop / thrift / op-shop card in `card-data.csv` or `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`; this is a net-new template.
- The pool currently has **30 business templates**; tier 2 contains Hardware Store (Service), Pawn Shop (Commerce) and Boutique (Commerce).
- Business cards are generic CSV-driven templates; `MainStreetCards.ts` parses rows, and per-tier registration is derived from the CSV `tier` column (`CARD_TIER_MAP`) — no bespoke TypeScript class is needed.
- Tests hardcode both the business-template count (`30`) **and aggregate pool totals** (tier-12 cumulative `173`, unique base-id set `165`), and `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` enumerates every non-baseline business id (currently 26 business ids; with the 4 tier-1 baseline business ids the total is 30) — all must be updated. `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` also hardcodes the per-tier synergy snapshot.
- Business card art resolves through `card-art-map.json` with a generic `Fallback` sprite when a dedicated 1024×1024 sprite is absent.

## Desired change

Add the Charity Shop as a tier-2 Culture business template with the values in AC1, regenerate the derived metadata and SVG card artifacts, update the hardcoded business-count assertions and the catalog documentation, and add/extend tests asserting the new card's economy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — add the `biz-charity-shop` business row.
- `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` — regenerate via `npx vite-node src/scripts/generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts` (business id list grows 26 → 27).
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-charity-shop.svg` — generated by `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — add the card to the tier-2 business table; update the two deck-size tables (Business 30 → 31, business cards 90 → 93), the expansion summary (Business 30 → 31, total 157 → 158, net +142 → +143) and the synergy-type coverage table (Culture single 4 → 5; Culture total 10 → 11).
- `tests/main-street/game-state.test.ts` — `BUSINESS_TEMPLATE_COUNT` 30 → 31.
- `tests/main-street/group-a-business-expansion.test.ts` — business template count 30 → 31 (and wording/comment).
- `tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts` — business template count 30 → 31 (and test description).
- `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts`, `group-c-investment-events-expansion.test.ts`, `group-d-incident-events-expansion.test.ts`, `group-e-upgrade-cards-expansion.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` — `createBusinessDeck(1).length` 30 → 31.
- `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` — tier-12 `cumulativeCardIds` 173 → 174 (test title/comment too) and `allBaseIds.size` 165 → 166.
- `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` — extend the hardcoded sparse-tier snapshot for `'tier-2'` with `Culture: 1` (and update the header comment); optionally add a Charity Shop synergy assertion.
- `tests/main-street/card-manifest.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/card-svg-coverage.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tier-family-balance.test.ts` — driven by the regenerated artifacts/CSV; verify they pass.
- `tests/main-street/card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — verifies card text matches data; passes once `description`/`art_notes` match the values in AC1.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — add a Special Cases note for the producer's manual cost override (if the balance doc is maintained against the CSV).

## Related work

> The `CG-` ids below are from the legacy Tableau-Card-Engine (core) worklog; the same content was migrated to this repo under the `MS-` prefix (see the migration comment on this item).

- `CG-0MUAYBA0L000XLK3` — Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (sibling migrated producer note; establishes the ×100 value convention for business cards).
- `CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6` — integer economy (coin/rep ×100).
- `CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE` — business ongoing cost (¼ purchase price, min 25).
- `CG-0MUIH30NQ0047W1I` — Reconcile event card text to integer data; `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0` — validate all card text.
- `CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB` — tier synergy-type balance rule (constrains tier-2 placement).
- `CG-0MT3C744B009DS84` / `CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143` — 12-tier progression and family rebalance.
- Automated related-work report: `CG-0MSQE2NLX003ADIY` (Main Street: design 50+ new cards), `CG-0MMJTGQFE1RL6VJA` (synergy icons in help panel).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q2):** synergy type is **Culture** (a charity shop might thematically read as Commerce; overridden by the producer's answer).
- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q3):** **tier 2, standalone** (`maxLevel = 1`, no upgrade chain).
- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q1):** 1.5 is **gross** `baseIncome`; the standard 75 ongoing cost applies on top (net 0.75/turn).
- **Assumption (not explicitly confirmed; low risk):** `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`, and house-style `description`/`art_notes` text; the card uses the generic fallback sprite until dedicated art is supplied.
- **Risk:** hardcoded business counts **and aggregate pool totals** are spread across many tests; missing one turns the suite red — the count updates are the largest part of the change.
- **Risk:** regenerating `expanded-card-manifest.json` and SVG artifacts produces large/generated diffs; regenerate via the documented scripts rather than hand-editing.
- **Scope-creep guard:** dedicated 1024×1024 artwork for the card is **out of scope**; if wanted, record it as a linked follow-up work item rather than expanding this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1: Are the stated numbers gross or net of the standard ongoing cost?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): A** — 1.5 is gross `baseIncome`; `baseIncome = 150`, `ongoingCost = 75`, net 0.75/turn. Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4` on this item.
- **Q2: Which synergy type should the Charity Shop belong to?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): C** — `Culture`. Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4`.
- **Q3: Which progression tier, and should it have an upgrade path?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): A** — `tier = 2`, standalone (`upgradePath = Charity Shop`, `maxLevel = 1`). Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4`.
- **Note:** these answers were carried over from the originating (core-repo) intake; the producer should confirm them alongside the corrected paths/counts at the next review.
- **Non-blocking assumptions:** `id`/`name`/`description`/`art_notes` and fallback-art usage were proposed in the questions comment and **not corrected** by the producer; they are treated as accepted defaults unless the producer objects.

# Write storylines — harden, document, and extend the Main Street storyline system

**Epic.** Producer decisions (2026-09-26): **Q1 = epic**; **Q2 = implement all
improvements now**; **Q3 = keep Main Street-specific, but design with an eye to
extracting into core-engine in future — cutting corners is acceptable now, but
do not make extraction impossible.**

## Problem statement

Main Street has a *rough* storyline implementation: incident event cards can
carry a dual choice (`hasChoices` / `acceptNextCardId` / `rejectNextCardId`)
and the player's Accept/Reject decision schedules the next card in a chain
(`CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128`). The mechanic works and is tested, but it is thin,
implicit, and undocumented:

- the branching model supports only binary choices with one successor per
  branch, with no storyline identity/grouping;
- there is no static validation — a dangling chain link is only logged at
  runtime (`Chain card X not found in card data.`);
- there is no authoring, validation, or visualisation tooling (chains are
  hand-edited inside a 155-row CSV);
- no documentation explains how storylines are created and managed; and
- storylines are invisible to players as stories — they see two opaque
  buttons and no memory of how their choices shaped events.

This makes storylines hard to extend safely and invisible as a source of
player agency.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — author, extend and balance storylines
  (new chains, retro-fitting existing incidents) without editing engine code,
  and see the shape of a storyline at a glance.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — need a documented, validated, and
  flexible data model with clear seams so storyline changes cannot silently
  break, and so the mechanic can later move to the core engine.
- **Players** — should feel their choices shape an unfolding story, with
  visible continuity (what they chose, what it led to, which thread is still
  running) rather than two opaque buttons.
- **AI / Monte Carlo** — need a decision policy that remains correct as the
  branching model and option counts grow.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to define a storyline declaratively and run a
  validator, so I know every branch resolves before I ship it."
- "As a developer, I want a documented storyline model and an authoring guide,
  so I can add a multi-step chain without reverse-engineering the engine."
- "As a player, I want a storyline journal that shows my past choices and what
  they led to, so my decisions feel like they build a narrative."
- "As a player, I want to know which story threads are still running, so
  recurring events feel connected rather than random."
- "As a producer, I want a prioritised roadmap of further storyline
  improvements, so I can schedule the next iteration."

## Scope areas (all to be implemented — Q2 = all now)

### A. Model & engine hardening (+ future extraction seam)

1. **Storyline identity/grouping** — optional `storylineId` (+ display
   `storylineTitle`) on `EventCard` and in the CSV, grouping chain cards into
   named storylines. Backward compatible.
2. **Generalised option model** — support an ordered list of options (each
   with a label, a successor card id, and an effect policy of apply/skip),
   while preserving legacy `hasChoices` / `acceptNextCardId` /
   `rejectNextCardId` semantics byte-for-byte.
3. **Extraction seam** — isolate storyline definitions, state and resolution
   behind a small game-agnostic interface/registry and pure functions, with
   migration notes, so the mechanic can move to `src/core-engine` later
   without rewriting callers. Corners may be cut, but the boundary must exist
   and be documented.
4. **Static validation** — every link resolves; no dangling, duplicate or
   unknown references; sinks and cycles are intentional. Validation fails
   loudly (non-zero exit), not just via a runtime log.
5. **Invariants preserved** — undo/redo, save/load (old saves load), deferred
   end-of-turn mutation, transcript shape and AI resolution stay correct for
   all option counts.

### B. Documentation

6. Canonical **`docs/main-street/storylines.md`**: concepts, data model + CSV
   columns, resolution lifecycle, AI policy, tooling usage, an end-to-end
   authoring walkthrough with a worked example, an authoring checklist, and a
   documented extraction path to core-engine.
7. **`docs/DEVELOPER.md`** and **`example-games/main-street/README.md`**
   cross-reference the doc and list the new CSV columns and scripts.
8. A **doc-drift test** asserts the docs exist and that documented chain
   examples match the shipped CSV.
9. A prioritised **future-improvements roadmap** (tooling + player agency)
   documenting anything deliberately deferred, with deferred ideas captured as
   work items.

### C. Tooling (implemented)

10. **Validator** — `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` + an npm script
    (`validate:storylines`), wired into the test suite / pre-push so
    regressions fail the build.
11. **Graph / manifest export** — tool to emit a storyline graph or manifest
    (`--format mermaid|json`) plus a committed generated artefact and a JSON
    schema.
12. **Authoring helper** — a CLI (or equivalent documented commands) to add and
    link storyline cards safely, without hand-editing CSV internals.

### D. Player agency (implemented)

13. **Named storylines surfaced** in the choice dialog and activity log.
14. **Storyline journal/history overlay** — review past choices and outcomes,
    accessible from the HUD, using the standard overlay pattern and
    reduced-motion behaviour, backed by the existing transcript/log.
15. **Choice clarity** — explanatory tooltips/labels for each option that
    explain consequence semantics **without** revealing the escalation card
    (preserving the designed tension).
16. **Outcome feedback** — each resolved choice produces a concise narrative
    "story update" line tied to its `storylineId`.
17. **Continuity / foreshadowing** — an active/recurring-thread indicator while
    a storyline is in play (including cycles).

## Acceptance Criteria

### Model & engine

1. **Storyline metadata** — `EventCard` (and the CSV) supports an optional
   `storylineId` and `storylineTitle`; the parser populates them; cards
   without them behave exactly as before. Covered by unit tests.
2. **Generalised option model** — the engine supports an arbitrary ordered
   list of options (label, successor card id, effect policy apply/skip);
   legacy `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` cards resolve
   identically. Covered by unit tests proving legacy-equivalence and a
   multi-option resolution.
3. **Extraction seam** — storyline definition/state/resolution are behind a
   documented game-agnostic interface/registry boundary with pure functions
   and explicit migration notes in the docs; no caller reaches into
   Main-Street-only internals for resolution.
4. **Static validation passes** — every `acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId`
   (and any new option link) in `card-data.csv` resolves to an existing card;
   no dangling/duplicate/unknown references; validation exits non-zero on
   failure and is enforced in the test suite or pre-push hook.
5. **Invariants preserved** — undo/redo, save/load (old saves without new
   fields load), deferred end-of-turn mutation, transcript `event-choice`
   records, and AI resolution remain correct for all option counts; covered by
   unit tests.

### Documentation

6. **Canonical documentation** — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` exists and
   documents concepts, the data model and CSV columns, the resolution
   lifecycle (deferred `pendingEventChoice`, option paths, deck insertion,
   undo/redo, save/load, transcript), the AI policy, tooling usage, a
   step-by-step authoring walkthrough with a worked example, an authoring
   checklist, and the core-engine extraction path.
7. **Cross-references updated** — `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and
   `example-games/main-street/README.md` reference the new doc and list the new
   CSV columns and scripts.
8. **Doc-drift guard** — at least one test/lint asserts the canonical doc
   exists and that its documented chain examples match the shipped CSV.
9. **Future-improvements roadmap** — the documentation contains a prioritised
   roadmap of further tooling and player-agency improvements, and any deferred
   ideas are captured as separate work items.

### Tooling

10. **Validator script** — `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` plus an npm script
    (`validate:storylines`), returning non-zero on invalid storylines and
    covered by tests against both valid and deliberately broken fixtures.
11. **Graph/manifest export** — a tool emits the storyline graph/manifest
    (`--format mermaid|json`); a generated artefact and JSON schema are
    committed, and a test asserts the emitted graph matches the CSV.
12. **Authoring helper** — a documented CLI (or equivalent) can add a
    storyline card/link safely and validate the result; the workflow is covered
    by the authoring guide and at least one test.

### Player agency

13. **Named storylines surfaced** — the choice dialog and activity log show the
    storyline name (e.g. "Tax Troubles — …") when available, with a
    reduced-motion-safe presentation.
14. **Journal/history overlay** — a player can open a storyline journal from
    the HUD that lists past choices and their outcomes; it uses
    `createOverlayBackground`/`createOverlayButton`, parents elements into
    `hudContainer`, and is covered by a browser test.
15. **Choice clarity** — option buttons carry tooltips/labels explaining
    consequence semantics without revealing the escalation card; covered by a
    test.
16. **Outcome feedback** — each resolved choice emits a concise narrative
    "story update" line tied to its storyline; covered by a unit test.
17. **Continuity indicator** — an active/recurring-storyline indicator is
    visible while a storyline is in play and cleared when it ends; covered by a
    test.

### Quality gates

18. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
    code comments, `README`, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
19. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility** — cards without storyline fields behave exactly
  as before; existing `hasChoices` cards are unchanged; old saves load with
  missing fields defaulted.
- **Determinism / replay safety** — storyline resolution and chain-card
  insertion must not consume RNG or wall-clock time; transcripts stay
  replayable and deterministic.
- **No cost model change** — event choices remain free (no daily-action cost).
- **Preserve designed tension** — choice clarity must not preview the
  escalation card; the "unknown consequence" tension is intentional.
- **Extraction seam, not extraction** — the mechanic stays Main Street-specific
  for now; corners may be cut but the boundaries must not make a later move to
  `src/core-engine` a rewrite.
- **Existing event-flow decisions preserved** — deferred end-of-turn mutation,
  undo/redo semantics, AI difficulty policy and tutorial exclusion of choice
  events must not regress.
- **No new runtime dependency** beyond the existing Node/Vitest/scripts
  toolchain for the tooling.

## Existing state (repo research)

### Data model
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `EventCard` has
  `hasChoices?: boolean`, `acceptNextCardId?: string | null`,
  `rejectNextCardId?: string | null` (`DurationEventCard` inherits them).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — header already contains the three
  columns. **7 choice cards** ship: `evt-tax` (→ `evt-tax-inquiry`), `evt-flu-outbreak`
  (→ `evt-pandemic`), `evt-recession` (→ `evt-depression`), `evt-tax-error`
  (→ `evt-tax`), `evt-tax-inquiry` (→ `evt-tax-error` on accept — a cycle),
  `evt-strike-service` (→ `evt-general-strike`), `evt-popular-menu`
  (→ `evt-farm-table`). Four terminal escalation cards ship
  (`evt-tax-inquiry` is itself a choice card).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` parses the three CSV
  columns into typed fields.

### Engine / lifecycle
- `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveIncident()` intercepts
  `hasChoices`, stashes `state.pendingEventChoice` and returns `null`;
  `resolveEventChoice()` implements accept (apply + push `acceptNextCardId`)
  and reject (skip + push `rejectNextCardId`); `pushChainCard()` pushes a
  freshly built instance to the **top** of the incident deck with a
  deterministic serial; `processEndOfTurn()` pauses with
  `TurnResult.choicePending`.
- `MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — typed `PendingEventChoice` on `MainStreetState`
  (`{ event, chosenOption, resolved }`).
- `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialises/backfills `pendingEventChoice`.
- `MainStreetCommands.ts` — snapshot-based undo/redo of the choice.
- `MainStreetTranscript.ts` — records `{ type: 'event-choice', eventId,
  cardName, option, acceptNextCardId, rejectNextCardId }`.

### UI
- `scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showEventChoiceDialog(event,
  onAccept, onReject)` (Accept/Reject buttons, no escalation preview, overlay
  depth conventions).
- `scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — shows the dialog when
  `choicePending` is observed; reduced-motion aware.

### AI
- `MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice(state, event, difficulty)`
  (Easy: always accept; Medium: accept if manageable; Hard: static full-chain
  severity comparison + `AI_EVENT_CHOICE_SIGNIFICANTLY_WORSE_RATIO`).
- `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `resolveAiEventChoice()` resolves pending choices
  in headless/AI turns.

### Tests
- `tests/main-street/chain-content.test.ts`, `event-choice*.test.ts`,
  `MainStreetEventChoice*.test.ts`, `MainStreetAiEventChoice.test.ts`,
  `ai-choice.test.ts`, `tutorial-choice-exclusion.test.ts`,
  `event-choice-dialog*.browser.test.ts`, `incident-*.test.ts`.

### Gaps observed
- **No documentation** of the storyline model or authoring process in `docs/`
  (only a passing mention in `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`).
- **No static validation tooling** — dangling links only logged at runtime.
- **No authoring/visualisation tooling** — no schema, generator or graph view.
- **Binary-only branching** and **no storyline identity/history/journal**.
- **Content child still open** — `CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58` ("Content: New chain
  cards and retro-fitting") is `status=open`, `stage=plan_complete`, despite
  the chain content appearing to ship; reconcile it.

## Desired change

1. **Harden** the model: add storyline identity, static validation, and fix
   code-comment/documentation gaps; reconcile the open content child.
2. **Generalise, with a seam**: support an ordered option list while preserving
   legacy accept/reject, behind a documented game-agnostic boundary that can
   later move to `src/core-engine`.
3. **Document** the full lifecycle end to end for content designers and
   developers.
4. **Implement** the tooling (validator, graph/manifest export, authoring
   helper) and player-agency improvements (named storylines, journal, clarity,
   feedback, continuity indicator).
5. **Test** the hardened model, tooling and player-facing behaviour, and guard
   against doc/code drift.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — **new** canonical documentation.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — cross-reference / short summary section.
- `example-games/main-street/README.md` — CSV column reference + scripts.
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — storyline metadata + links.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — model + extraction seam
  types.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — CSV parsing.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — resolution,
  `pushChainCard`, option-list support.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `PendingEventChoice`
  shape.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — dialog,
  journal overlay, tooltips.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — HUD
  wiring for the journal/continuity indicator.
- `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — **new** validator.
- `scripts/storyline-graph.ts` (or similar) + `schemas/…storyline…json` —
  **new** export + schema.
- `tests/main-street/` — model, validator, tooling, player-agency and
  doc-drift tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk (epic)** — "implement all improvements now" is broad; the epic
  must be decomposed into independently reviewable children so a stalled slice
  does not block the rest. *Mitigation:* plan will break this into
  vertical slices.
- **Over-engineering risk** — the generalised option model could destabilise a
  shipped mechanic. *Mitigation:* legacy-equivalence tests; accept/reject
  remains a first-class compatibility path.
- **Extraction-seam drift** — the seam could decay into Main-Street-only

- **CG-0MU1SJ6D2008WAW2** — "[test-failure] npm test failing" (`open`,

# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

## Summary

Add a hover tooltip to the persistent synergy lines drawn between adjacent
synergistic businesses on the Main Street board. Hovering a line explains the
shared synergy type and the per-turn effect that link has on each of the two
connected cards.

## User Story

As a Main Street player, I want to hover over a synergy line and see what that
synergy does — the shared type and the coins/reputation each linked business
gains from it — so that I can understand *why* two businesses are connected and
plan my street deliberately, instead of guessing from the line colour alone.

## Problem Statement

The board draws coloured synergy lines between adjacent businesses that share a
synergy type, but the lines are purely decorative: hovering them does nothing.
The player sees that two cards are linked but not which synergy type they share,
the rate that applies, or the value of that specific connection. The only
synergy information available today is the per-card `Synergy: <types>` line in
the business-slot tooltip, which does not explain the link or its magnitude.

## Existing State

- `drawSynergyLines()` in
  `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` draws a
  two-pass `Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics` line (core + glow) per synergy pair and
  adds it to `streetContainer`. The graphics objects are **not interactive** —
  there is no input handler on them.
- `computeSynergyPairs()` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyNeighbors.ts`
  returns `SynergyPair { fromIndex, toIndex, sharedSynergy }`, the data the
  renderer iterates to draw each line. Sold cards still participate as pair
  endpoints (CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ).
- Per-card synergy maths lives in
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`:
  `computeSynergyBonus()` (coin), `computeSynergyRepBonus()` (reputation),
  `effectiveSynergyCoinBonus()` / `effectiveSynergyRepBonus()`. The difficulty
  multiplier is `config.synergyBonusPerNeighbor`.
- Existing formatting helpers live in
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` (`effectiveSynergyRate()`,
  `formatSynergyRate()`, `formatPerTurnReputation()`, `formatCurrency()`).
- Business-slot tooltips already use the shared `TooltipManager`
  (`s.tooltipManager?.show(info, x, y)` / `.hide()`); the manager is created
  only when `!s.replayMode`
  (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`) and already honours the
  `settingsPanel.showTooltips` toggle.

## Desired Change

1. Add a pure, unit-testable content builder — e.g.
   `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo(grid, fromIndex, toIndex, sharedSynergy, config, soldSlots?, gridDims?)`
   in `MainStreetFormatting.ts` — that returns the tooltip text for one link.
2. In `drawSynergyLines()`, give each line a **narrow, invisible interactive hit
   area** (parented into `streetContainer`, drawn/recreated with the rest of the
   street layer) wired to `tooltipManager.show(...)` on `pointerover` and
   `tooltipManager.hide()` on `pointerout`.
3. Guard the wiring the same way existing slot tooltips are: no tooltip in
   `replayMode` and no tooltip when `tooltipManager` is absent; the
   `showTooltips` setting continues to be enforced by `TooltipManager` itself.
4. Ensure the hit area does not swallow the existing business-slot hover/click
   interactions except immediately along the line (see Constraints).

### Suggested tooltip format (implementation may refine wording)

```
Food synergy
Bakery  ⟷  Diner
Bakery: +2 coins/turn from this link
Diner: +1 coins/turn from this link
+5 reputation/turn  (only when a reputation-synergy contribution exists)
```

Sold endpoints are called out explicitly, e.g.
`Bakery (sold): earns nothing, but still anchors this synergy`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hovering a persistent synergy line shows a tooltip that names the shared
  synergy type and states the per-turn coin and/or reputation effect of that
  link for **each** endpoint, computed with the active difficulty multiplier
  (`config.synergyBonusPerNeighbor`).
- The tooltip is hidden when the pointer leaves the line, and is not shown at
  all in replay mode; the existing `settingsPanel.showTooltips = false` toggle
  suppresses it (via `TooltipManager`).
- A sold endpoint is represented correctly: it earns nothing from the link
  itself, while the link still anchors synergy for the other endpoint, and the
  tooltip says so.
- The line hover hit area does not break the existing business-slot
  interactions: slot hover tooltips, click-to-place, sell, and upgrade
  targeting continue to work everywhere except the line's immediate vicinity.
- Unit tests cover the pure `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo()` builder (shared
  type, coin-only, reputation, sold endpoint, zero-synergy opt-out, difficulty
  multiplier) and an automated test covers the hover wiring on a rendered line.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the shared `TooltipManager` (`@ui`) — do **not** add a bespoke tooltip
  renderer, consistent with
  [Standardize TooltipManager across all games] (CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44) and
  [Tooltip single-source fix] (CG-0MTJP6RNL008LGF3).
- Keep the content builder **pure** (no Phaser/scene dependency) so it can be
  unit-tested headless, mirroring `synergyLineEndpoints.ts`.
- Synergy lines are drawn **after** the slot rectangles in `drawSynergyLines()`,
  so their hit areas sit on top of the slot hit zones. The hit area must be
  narrow (a thin band around the segment, thick enough for a mouse but not so
  thick that it steals slot hover) and the chosen thickness/approach must be
  documented in a code comment.
- Hit areas are recreated on every `streetContainer` rebuild (the street layer
  is rebuilt by `refreshAll()`), so their creation must not leak listeners or
  leave stale objects behind.
- Reduced-motion: no animation is introduced; the tooltip appears/hides
  immediately, so reduced-motion preferences are unaffected.
- No new engine-level (`src/`) API is expected — Main Street-local formatting +
  renderer wiring only.
- Out of scope: tooltips on the transient synergy-formation animation line,
  changing the synergy formula, and changing line geometry/colours.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — Add an
  interactive hit area per synergy pair inside `drawSynergyLines()` and wire it
  to `s.tooltipManager`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — New pure
  `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo()` builder (shared synergy type + per-endpoint
  coin/reputation effect).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — Reuse/extract the
  per-link contribution maths if a per-neighbour share helper is needed
  (avoid duplicating the synergy formula).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyNeighbors.ts` — Source of
  `SynergyPair`; may need no change beyond typing.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-tooltip.test.ts` — New unit tests for the content
  builder.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-tooltip.browser.test.ts` — New browser test for
  hover wiring (or extend `tests/main-street/synergy-visuals.test.ts`).
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — Document the synergy-line tooltip
  interaction.
- `example-games/main-street/README.md` — Mention the tooltip in the synergy
  overview (if the README describes synergy lines).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption (documented, producer may adjust):** "the effect of that synergy"
  means the shared type plus the per-link per-turn coin/reputation contribution
  for each endpoint, rather than a generic rules paragraph. The suggested
  format above is a proposal; wording can change without altering the ACs.
- **Risk — per-link vs. card-total mismatch:** `computeSynergyBonus()` rounds
  the *total* across all matching neighbours, so a per-link share may not sum
  exactly to the displayed card total. The tooltip must not imply a precision
  it does not have; document the chosen presentation (per-link share formatted
  to at most one decimal, or card total) in the builder's doc comment.
- **Risk — input interception:** adding interactive objects on top of the slot
  hit zones can regress slot hover/click. Mitigation: narrow hit band + an
  explicit regression test for slot hover/click; keep the band culled with the
  line.
- **Risk — re-render churn:** `drawSynergyLines()` runs on every refresh; a
  fresh hit area per refresh must be destroyed with the container or it leaks.
- **Scope-creep guard:** any desire to also tooltip the *animated* formation
  line, restyle lines, or change synergy values must be filed as a separate
  work item, not folded into this one.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MM4REC2Z0GS2YKT** – Main Street: PRD Milestone 2 -- Full Content and Crafting/Building System (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHCJJ5009AB4X** – Fix Lighting Spike scene visibility (completed)
- **CG-0MQOBJ9BW006TTJR** – Main Street score tooltip should show calculation breakdown (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)
- `example-games/gym/README.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)

### Manual related references

- **CG-0MQQHBZ3D002J02E** – Add visual synergy lines between adjacent businesses
  (completed): introduced the lines this work item makes interactive.
- **CG-0MSVM3WCD007BRQP** – Synergy lines drawn edge-to-edge / corner-to-corner
  (completed): `synergyLineEndpoints.ts` geometry reused for the hit band.
- **CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ** – Main Street sold businesses still provide synergy
  (completed): defines sold-endpoint semantics the tooltip must reflect.
- **CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44** – Standardize TooltipManager across all games
  (completed): the shared tooltip component to reuse.
- **CG-0MTJP6RNL008LGF3** – Tooltip single-source fix (completed): tooltip
  content should come from shared formatters.
- **CG-0MT5Y9AD2001MKWZ** – Tooltips on businesses are confusing (completed):
  precedent for clarifying Main Street tooltip wording.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — synergy line visual/audio spec
  (lines, coin flights, animation) to extend with the tooltip.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was required: the seed context and the existing
Main Street code path (`drawSynergyLines` → `SynergyPair` → per-card synergy
formula → `TooltipManager`) were sufficient to draft a clear brief. The single
open design decision was resolved by documented assumption:

- **Assumption A1 (tooltip content):** the tooltip shows the shared synergy
  type and the per-link per-turn coin/reputation contribution for each
  endpoint, rather than a generic rules sentence. Rationale: this matches the
  wording "showing the effect of that synergy" and the precedent set by
  [Add scoring tooltip to expedition column headers] (CG-0MLXCSSES11VPL3C),
  which surfaces the live contribution rather than a definition. Source:
  repo evidence (`SynergyPair.sharedSynergy`, `computeSynergyBonus`,
  `computeSynergyRepBonus`). **OPEN QUESTION for the producer:** confirm the
  proposed format, or specify an alternative (e.g. show the card's *total*
  synergy bonus instead of the per-link share).

# Intake Brief — Move level label to left (MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327)

## Problem Statement
When a business or community-space card is upgraded it shows a gold level badge
("Lvl 1", "Lvl 2", …) in the **top-right** corner of the card face. This
position competes with the cost circle / right-hand text column and reads as a
secondary stat rather than the card's primary upgrade indicator. The badge
should move to the **top-left** of the card so the upgrade level is immediately
visible in a consistent, expected position.

## Users
- **Main Street player** — wants to identify an upgraded card's level at a
  glance when scanning the street grid and their hand.
- **Future example-game authors / designers** — reuse the shared
  `UpgradeOverlaySpec` contract and expect a single, predictable corner
  convention for the level badge.

### User Stories
- As a player, when I look at an upgraded card on the street or in my hand, I
  see the "Lvl N" badge at the top-left of the card, so the level is obvious at
  a glance.
- As a player, the badge position is identical whether the card is shown on the
  street grid or in the hand, so I never have to re-learn where to look.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For every upgraded card (`level > 0`), the level badge is positioned at
      the card's **top-left**: in container-local coordinates (origin at the
      card centre) `levelBadge.x` is negative (left of centre) and the badge is
      **left-anchored** (`originX === 0`); the badge is no longer placed in the
      top-right (`x` must not be positive in the mirrored position). Verified by
      unit test on `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec` for level 1 and level 2 cards.
- [ ] The Phaser renderer (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) renders the badge with a
      left/top origin so the text starts at the top-left inset and remains fully
      inside the card bounds (no clipping past the left or top edge); the same
      overlay path is used by street and hand cards, so both move together.
      Verified by renderer/overlay tests.
- [ ] Badge content and styling are unchanged (`Lvl N`, gold `#ffdd44`, bold,
      10px) and no badge is produced for level 0 (base) cards.
- [ ] The dynamic SVG card-face generator (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits the
      level badge at the top-left (`x` at the card's left inset,
      `text-anchor="start"`) for consistency with the overlay, with its unit
      tests updated accordingly.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
      (notably the module docs in `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` /
      `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and the level-badge references in
      `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, with all existing
      top-right level-badge expectations updated to the top-left contract.

## Constraints
- Card geometry is fixed: canonical **140 × 80** card with a **64 × 64 art zone
  at (8, 8)** (top-left) — see `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md`. The
  top-left corner is therefore occupied by the card art; the badge will render
  over the top-left of the art zone (mirroring the current badge overlaying the
  top-right). This is an accepted input to the brief (see Risks & Assumptions).
- Presentation-only change — no change to upgrade rules, card state, or level
  numbers.
- Reuse the existing overlay/badge primitives and gold styling; do not introduce
  new assets or a second badge component.
- Keep the overlay spec a pure data module (no Phaser imports) so it stays
  unit-testable in Node.

## Existing State
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` builds the badge at
  `x = Math.round(width / 2 - 4)`, `y = Math.round(4 - height / 2)` (top-right,
  4 px inset) with `color: '#ffdd44'`, `fontSize: '10px'`, `fontStyle: 'bold'`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) creates the
  Phaser Text and calls `lvlText.setOrigin(1, 0)` — right/top anchored — so the
  badge sits in the top-right.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits
  `<text x="${width - 8}" y="13" … text-anchor="end">Lvl N</text>` (top-right)
  for upgraded cards. (This dynamic SVG path is exercised by unit tests; the
  runtime card face texture comes from the CSV-based template SVGs.)
- Tests asserting/pinning the badge: `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts`
  (positions the badge in the top-right), `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts`
  and `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` (badge presence/text),
  `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` (badge text).

## Desired Change
- Mirror the badge to the top-left: overlay `x = Math.round(-width / 2 + 4)`
  with `originX: 0` (and `setOrigin(0, 0)` in the renderer); `y` stays at the
  existing top inset so the badge remains on the top edge.
- Update the SVG generator badge to `x = 8` (or the chosen left inset) with
  `text-anchor="start"`.
- Update the module/JSDoc comments and the affected tests from "top-right" to
  "top-left". Exact inset values may be tuned during implementation as long as
  the badge is left-anchored in the top-left and stays inside the card bounds.

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — level-badge spec `x` / `originX` and the
  "top-right corner" comment; primary change.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `applyUpgradeOverlays` badge
  `setOrigin(1, 0)` → `(0, 0)`; comment.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — dynamic SVG badge position /
  `text-anchor`; module doc mentions "level badge top-right".
- `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` — update the top-right
  position assertion to top-left and assert left-anchoring.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` — badge position/style
  expectations.
- `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — badge presence/absence
  alongside the cash line (position regression surface).
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — SVG badge text/position.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — level-badge placement references.

## Related Work
- **Potentially related docs:**
  - `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — canonical 140×80 card and the
    `(8, 8)` 64×64 art zone that occupies the top-left.
  - `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — upgrade level-up burst notes that
    reference the newly-rendered level badge.
  - `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` header — documents the overlay contract
    and the card-local coordinate system.
- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `MS-0MTV69NII000LW8I` — *Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card,
    growing right* (bug, medium) — closest precedent: a card-face overlay
    repositioned from centre/right to left, landed with documented placement
    assumptions.
  - `MS-0MU9JYNZ3008AH5J` — *Update createCoinGrid defaults to left-anchored
    position* (task) — companion implementation task for the sister reposition.
  - `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — *Assign a dedicated 64×64 sprite to every Main
    Street card* (medium) — touches the top-left art zone that the badge will
    now overlay.
  - `MS-0MTRRYOT6001167R` — *Change the name of Physiotherapy business card to
    Physiotherapist* (task, low) — another card-face presentation tweak with
    test/doc churn.
  - Historical (core-repo) references cited in code: `CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN`
    (64×64 left-art layout) and `CG-0MP1VJVEK003I7VE` (display upgrade state on
    street-grid cards) — the layout and overlay these tests assert were
    introduced/refined there.
- **Automated report** (generated by `find-related`) — see the
  "Related work (automated report)" section retained below.

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Assumption:** "top left" means the card's top-left corner, mirroring the
  current right-side inset, with the badge left-aligned. Because the 64×64 art
  zone occupies `(8, 8)`–`(72, 72)`, the badge will overlay the top-left of the
  card art. That is accepted; if the producer finds it illegible over the art, a
  subtle backing chip or a slightly different inset is a small follow-up — it
  must be raised rather than assumed.
- **Visual-regression risk:** the badge colour (`#ffdd44` gold) may have low
  contrast against some card art; mitigate during implementation by checking the
  darkest/lightest card arts and, if needed, a 1 px dark outline (recorded as a
  follow-up if it expands scope).
- **Test churn:** `upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` explicitly asserts a
  top-right position; update the assertions to the top-left contract in the same
  change rather than deleting them.
- **Scope creep:** do not restyle the badge, redesign the 64×64 layout, or
  change the cost circle / title / cash line. Record any broader card-face polish
  as separate work items.

## Open Questions
- None — the seed context (position the upgrade level badge at the top-left
  instead of the top-right) plus repo inspection of the overlay/spec/renderer
  provided sufficient signal for a clear brief. The only judgement call (badge
  overlays the top-left art zone) is recorded above as an assumption to be
  confirmed during review; no clarifying interview was required.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers
- No interview conducted — the work-item description ("When a card is upgraded
  it gets a 'Lvl 1' label. Move this from the current location (top right) to
  the top left.") plus repo inspection of `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`,
  `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, and `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` provided
  sufficient signal to draft a clear brief. No assumptions were left
  unrecorded; see Risks & Assumptions for the documented top-left-art-overlay
  assumption.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** – write storylines (open)
- **MS-0MTIILDBB001F01S** – Competitive Monte Carlo harness: head-to-head simulation (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** – Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: card, current, gets, label, left, level, location, lvl, move, right, top, upgraded, when
- `core/docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — matched: card, current, gets, left, level, location, move, right, top, upgraded, when
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: card, current, gets, label, left, level, move, right, top, upgraded, when
